title: Accelerator Architectures for Machine Learning
description:
Machine learning has captured tremendous successes to solve difficult learning problems. Hardware accelerators pursue continued performance and energy-efficient gains to meet the intensive computation in machine learning applications. This course explores leading approaches that tackle machine learning computational challenges and have been emerged in industrial and academic research. This course aims to build up students a foundation to understand the programming and accelerator architectural functions.
This course begins with the fundamental basis of deep neural networks (DNN). The second potion of this course provides students accelerator hardware architectures specified for machine learning workloads. This course will address the graphic processing units (GPUs) that are widely used for the training of the neural networks and specialized machine learning accelerators such as tensor processor units (TPUs). The final portion of this course discusses challenges in designing accelerator architectures for machine learning applications and introduces emerging accelerator architectures.
This course includes the programming assignments to use the computer architecture simulator, research paper reading and a class project to reflect ideas that improve accelerator architecture designs.

title: Formal Languages and Theory of Computation
description:
The Ultimate Question: What inherently makes some problems computationally effortless while others remain frustratingly difficult?
Despite five decades of intense research, computer scientists still don't have a definitive answer to this question. However, this pursuit has yielded a massive breakthrough: an elegant classification framework that categorizes problems based on their intrinsic difficulty.
This theoretical blueprint has directly revolutionized the ancient field of cryptography. By intentionally building security systems around these certified "hard" problems, cryptographers have successfully engineered entirely new, ultra-secure codes.

title: Algorithms
description:
Shall know the way to design efficient algorithms and analyze the time and space complexity of algorithms. Some advance data structures those are needed to design efficient algorithms. Introduce some graph algorithms. To a computational problem, is it tractable (NP)? Or how fast we can solve it (lower bound).
Courses will cover
1. An introduction, sorting algorithms, asymptotic notations, recursion, 2 to 3 weeks.
2. \Omega(n log n) Lower bound to sorting algorithm, Why there are sorting algorithms beat this lower bound. 1 week,
3. Selection, a computational problem similar to but easier than sorting.
4. Review the way to design algorithms, iteration, divide and conquer, randomize, prune and search.
5. Random variable and analysis of quick sort.
6. balance tree, red-black tree,
7. Other ways to design efficient algorithms, greedy approach, dynamic programming, amortized analysis,
8. Heap structures, binomial heap, Fibonacci Heap
9. Union/Find operations, Function that grows very fast or very slowly.
10. graph algorithms, Minimum Spanning Tree, BFS, DFS, application of DFS.
11. Some graph algorithms are not tractable, NP
12. hopefully, some computational geometry, parallel algorithms, FFT, Linear programming, ...

title: Network Security
description: This is the first course for all students who are interested in network security.  Students can learn the fundamental theory and practice of network security.

title: Complier Design
description:
This course is intended to explore the principal ideas and techniques of compiler construction. Topics include lexical analysis, syntax analysis including LL and LR parsers, type checking, run-time environments, symbol tables, code generation, and compiler-construction tools. Some compiler optimization techniques will also be covered.
This course aims to give you a solid foundation in the theory of compiler construction as well as the experience of building a compiler. Much of what you have learned about algorithms and data structures will come to bear as you study and implement the various components of a compiler. In a sense, compiler construction is a showcase for many other disciplines of computer science.
Course Objectives:
(1) To learn structure of compilers.
(2) To learn techniques used in compiler construction such as lexical analysis, top-down and bottom-up parsing, context-sensitive analysis, intermediate code generation, and code optimization.
(3) To learn basic data structures used in compiler construction such as abstract syntax trees, symbol tables, three-address code, and stack machines.
(4) To learn software tools used in compiler construction such as lexical analyzer generators (Lex), and parser generators (Yacc).
(5) To construct a compiler for a small language using the above techniques and tools.

title: Brain-Computer Interface
description:
Course outline:
This course explores state-of-the-art brain-sensing methodology and its application to neuroscience, neurology, and human-machine interaction. Lectures will be given on the relevant topics including the background to brain function, sensing technology, signal processing, machine learning methods, and applications of brain-computer interfacing (BCI) in various domains.
Course objectives:
1. Understand the background to conduct research in neuromonitoring and BCI.
2. Understand the literature in the field of BCI.
3. Understand and use engineering approaches in BCI.
4. Be able to apply tools required for real-time BCI systems.
5. Understand the domains and contexts in which BCIs are effective.
6. Understand the open questions and challenges in real-world applications of BCI.

title: Computer Networks
description: The course covers concepts in networking, including packet switching; Internet routing; IPv4 and IPv6 addressing; 5G, router, switch, and middlebox design; content distribution networks; wireless networks; datacenter networks; network security; software-defined networks;.

title: Computer Architecture
description:
The slowdown of transistor scaling has led to diminishing performance improvements in standard computer systems. With the loss of exponentially increasing resources provided by semiconductor scaling, computer architects are facing significant challenges in maintaining the growth of computing power.
This course begins with an introduction to advanced topics in conventional computer architecture and then explores the trends resulting from the end of Dennard Scaling and Moore's Law. These trends include the shift towards parallel computer architectures and systems, the integration of specialized and heterogeneous components, and the emergence of new hardware and software systems.

title: Seminars
description: This seminar-oriented course consists of a series of invited talks given by researchers and developers from universities, research institutes, and companies. The invited talks basically focus on the leading edge networking technology, including 5G Mobile Broadband Network (5G), Internet of Things (IoT), Big Data, Software Defined Network (SDN), Fog and Edge computing, and Machine Learning (ML).

title: Game Theory and Its Applications
description:
1. Acquire knowledge related to basic types of games (cooperative games, non-cooperative games, auctions, and matching theory).
2. Be able to formulate  problems in the network and distributed systems (including computing or networking resource allocations, bandwidth or channel contentions, and other problem involving mutual competition or cooperation) as games
3. Be able to design distributed, adaptive, and autonomous approaches to related problems based on game models.

title: Computer Vision
description: The goal of this course is to introduce the essential concepts and techniques of computer vision, from camera models, feature extraction, to high-level applications. Recent advances in computer vision based on deep learning will also be described.

title: Deep Learning
description:
1. To learn the mathematics of deep learning techniques
2. To become familiar with deep learning tools, such as PyTorch or TensorFlow
3. To gain a solid understanding of the latest developments and applications of deep learning techniques
4. To develop practical deep learning systems

title: Deep Learning Labs
description:
1. To learn the mathematics of deep learning techniques
2. To become familiar with deep learning tools, such as PyTorch or TensorFlow
3. To gain a solid understanding of the latest developments and applications of deep learning techniques

title: Memory and Storage Systems
description:
隨著大數據系統分析及類神經網路應用的盛行，記憶體與儲存系統的存取成為效能瓶頸。本課程將從計算機架構(包含運算單元、記憶體設備、儲存設備)以及作業系統 的演進切入，並探討兩者設計的相互關係。本課程將進一步探討，當今記憶體與儲存系統將如何演進，以及該如何跟大數據分析及類神經網路等應用程式垂直整合以解決效能瓶頸。
Data movements between computing and I/O devices become performance bottlenecks while running data-intensive applications, such as big data analysis and neural networks. This course is going to introduce new memory and storage technologies to break the bottleneck. We will cover several cool topics, such as next-generation non-volatile memory, co-designing between applications and devices, and near data computing.

title: Blockchain Development and FinTech
description:
授課教師：李嵩聲（Quantstamp Head of Developer Relations / Senior Research Engineer）
課程概述與目標：
Blockchain technology enables a publicly verifiable ledger to exist on top of the internet. Started as a grassroots movement from cryptographers, it now has become a valid infrastructure for financial assets. In this course we quickly go over the history and basic concepts of blockchain, and dive deep into smart contract development on EVM, the dominant smart contract execution environment that has been adopted by most chains. Along the way, we will discuss different financial infrastructures that have been built and how they have been attacked. Finally, we will touch on concepts outside of smart contract development such as MEV, Layer 2, Privacy that are being push forward in the blockchain industry.
區塊鏈科技使得公開可驗證帳簿之基礎設施得以存在於網路上。由密碼學家的草根運動開始的區塊鏈科技現已經成為重要而不可忽視的金融系統基礎設施。在這個課程中我們會從區塊鏈的緣起以及基本概念介紹起，然後藉由已經在鏈上存在的應用程式來深入探討基於EVM的智能合約開發。最後我們會快速介紹在智能合約開發以外的重要且正在被推進的觀念，如 MEV、Layer 2、隱私等等。

title: Mobile Network Security
description: This course introduces the fundamentals and applications of 5G cyber security,  and its research studies. The topics include legacy 3G/4G fundamentals and security, 5G fundamentals, 5G security (trust model, authentication, SBA, privacy, key hierarchy, etc.), security of 5G critical technologies (IoT, MEC, IMS, etc.), and research studies of 5G security in top conferences.

title: Medical Image Processing
description: 本課程主要教授醫學影像相關處理方法以及背景知識，並將以實際不同種類的醫學影像，如X光影像、CT影像、內視鏡影像、病理影像為例，引導學生瞭解醫學影像獨特的問題以及臨床的困難，並使用所學技術開發協助醫師診斷癌症、癌前病變與特定疾病之醫學影像處理方法，以解決醫學影像處理的實務問題。

title: Memory/Storage Systems Optimization & Implementation
description: 隨著大數據系統分析及類神經網路應用的盛行，記憶體與儲存系統的存取成為效能瓶頸。本課程將從計算機架構(包含運算單元、記憶體設備、儲存設備)以及作業系統 的演進切入，並探討兩者設計的相互關係。本課程將聚焦在探討產業界及學術界目前主流的多種架構與應用整合的議題，並以小組討論模式，幫助學生了解各種架構間的差異。

title: Advanced File System
description:
本課程將深入介紹檔案系統與鍵值儲存系統之作用原理與設計哲學，課程主軸涵蓋：(1) 輸出/輸入設備 (2) 檔案系統基礎與設計原理 (3) 檔案系統效能與可靠性優化 (4) 檔案系統一致性與故障恢復機制 (5) 分散式檔案系統設計與管理 (6) 鍵值儲存系統之設計與應用 (7) 檔案系統安全性與存取控制 (8) 檔案系統虛擬化與容器化應用。修習本課程之學生需具備作業系統、C 語言以及基礎 Linux 指令的先備知識。此外，本課程也將依據最新研究趨勢，探討現今最新的儲存裝置與檔案系統之相關研究，並深入探討鍵值儲存系統在高效能儲存系統與大數據管理領域的應用。
This course will explore the working principles and design philosophy of File Systems and Key-Value Stores, with a primary focus on: (1) I/O Devices, (2) File System Basics and Designs, (3) Performance and Reliability Optimization in File Systems, (4) File System Consistency and Crash Recovery Mechanisms, (5) Design and Management of Distributed File Systems, (6) Design and Applications of Key-Value Stores, (7) File System Security and Access Control, and (8) File System Virtualization and Containerization Applications. Students are expected to have foundational knowledge of Operating Systems, proficiency in the C language, and familiarity with basic Linux commands. Additionally, the course will introduce contemporary research trends and discuss advanced topics on storage devices, file systems, and the implementation and applications of key-value stores, particularly in the context of scalable and dependable big data management.

title: Physical AI
description:
Recent years have witnessed remarkable breakthroughs in artificial intelligence—from large language models transforming how humans interact with information to generative models capable of creating increasingly realistic images, videos, and virtual worlds. As AI continues to advance, the next major frontier extends beyond the digital world: Physical AI, where intelligent systems perceive, reason, make decisions, and act in the physical world.
Unlike AI systems operating primarily in digital spaces, Physical AI must confront the complexity and uncertainty of the physical world: incomplete observations, changing environments, embodiment constraints, sensor and actuator failures, interactions with people, and consequences associated with physical actions. This course introduces the foundations and recent advances of Physical AI through the lens of real-world development, evaluation, and deployment. Specifically, as AI moves into the physical world, we must continuously ask: What challenges emerge when the system leaves the benchmark and enters the real world? How should we evaluate a Physical AI system beyond predefined metrics and state-of-the-art performance? How can evaluation reveal system limitations and, more importantly, guide inference, system improvement, and future development?
Intended Learning Outcomes:
- Explain the recent advances of Physical AI
- Apply the Sense-Plan-Act paradigm to robotic navigation and manipulation
- Identify real-world challenges in the development and deployment of Physical AI systems beyond predefined benchmarks
- Recognize the critical role of evaluation beyond predefined metrics and state-of-the-art benchmark performance
- Apply evaluation insights to guide inference and system improvement by leveraging observed failures, limitations, and operating conditions to refine system design and behavior

title: Social Computing and Social Media Design
description:
(Please check the course website for the updated syllabus and schedule: https://bit.ly/nycu-social-computing-1142)
This course considers the broad design space of technology and software systems that aim to foster social interaction beyond the individual. The modern landscape of social technology has expanded to support communication and interaction among people with whom we have various types of relationships - from family, friends, co-workers, acquaintances, to complete strangers, people with shared and different interests and opinions. Furthermore, almost all of our work-related collaboration and cooperation is mediated through technology.
Technologies that facilitate social connections include social media platforms, messaging apps, such as Facebook, BeReal, Threads, Discord, Slack, and Dcard. These apps adopted different design elements including algorithmic recommendation systems, response (e.g., like, comment, repost, remix, ) and audience management features (e.g., "close friends"), and supporting different content modalities (e.g., text, image, video).  There is also a growing tendency for apps that traditionally focus on instrumental needs like tracking physical activities, managing finance and transactions, or listening to music to embed social features that are designed for engagement and social support goals.
As social technologies have changed the way we interact and connect with others, the advancements have led to both opportunities and challenges, such as privacy-related issues and online harms. How do we design social computing systems to be effective and responsible?
This course covers emerging topics related to the modern landscape of social computing system design, including the design spaces of application and platforms, the foundational social scientific and technical knowledge that underpins them. You will engage in activities to learn about core concepts, and practice and apply them through working on assignments and group project designed to help gain hands-on experiences for understanding current issues within the field.
At the end of this course, you should be able to:
- Relate social scientific and technological concepts to the design of social computing systems
- Describe canonical intellectual agendas of CSCW and Social Computing, and articulate how a new paper in the space contributes to one or more of the agendas.
- Identify how the design of social computing systems may generate potential social benefits and harms.
- Make a scholarly contribution to the field of CSCW and Social Computing, and relate the topic to your own research interests.

title: Research on Cybersecurity and AI
description:
資安領域因為AI的導入讓防守方的籃隊與攻擊方的紅隊都提升能力，對藍隊而言，AI讓偵測更有彈性與通用性，對紅隊而言，AI讓技法與攻擊路徑的選擇更像人類甚至超越人類，不論哪一方，不使用AI解決資安問題都會陷入武器不對等的困境。在使用AI的過程，AI本身也變成攻擊表面，因此也需要被防護，近年來AI的發展已形成模型在後端、agent在前端的架構，前後端都可能被攻擊，也發展出類似SQL injection的prompt injection等攻擊模式。
以上兩群的研究都是資安及AI領域的熱門研究議題，本課程將透過資安、AI、資安AI、AI資安四個單元的介紹，以及近兩年內高度相關的論文集，引導學生發展自己的碩博士論文的計畫書 (proposal)，學生在期中做一次較簡單的pre-proposal報告，內含problem, solution ideas, comparative survey，來初步篩選過濾不適合的題目，經過換題目或修改題目後定案，在期末做一次較詳細的proposal報告，內含motivation, background, issues, problem statement, survey, solution, implementation plan, experiment plan, schedule, reference，來定錨論文最重要的proposal階段。學生除了可以學習到這四個領域的知識與技能，更能學習到研究方法，包含如何找出一個領域的問題空間、對此空間的現有研究歸類比較、找尋是否有足夠大的可貢獻空間、比較自己與現有研究在問題與解決方向的差異、精確定義與描述問題、強調與描述解決方案、規劃實作與實驗、設定待回答的議題等。

title: Practice in Entrepreneurship
description: This class is designed for students who might have the tendency to setup a business now or in the future.   We will guide you to accomplish a business proposal that can be used for future fund raising or a better understand of your business.

title: Biomedical Micro Analysis Systems
description:
Bio-lab on a chip (Bio-LOC) is a device that integrates several laboratory functions on a single chip; It deals with the handling of extremely small fluid volumes. Bio-LOC is closely related to, and overlaps with, microfluidics, which describes primarily the physics, the manipulation and study of minute amounts of fluids. The devices are a subset of MEMS devices and often indicated by "Micro Total Analysis Systems" (μTAS) as well. Several specific topics will be taught in this course that includes: 1. Microfluidic devices, 2. DNA microarrays, 3. Protein microarrays, 4. Nano-biosensor, 5. Single DAN sequence, and et al. The field of this course covers basic chemistry, biochemistry, nano-technology, semi-conductance-technology, and applications of these multidisciplinary sciences.
醫療科技的發展，個人化醫學的需求逐漸浮現。微小化、智慧化、高通量化與遠距化成為是技術的生醫發展的共同趨勢。本課程主旨在使同學對生物晶片有基本之認識，內容將涵蓋microfluidic devices, DNA microarrays，protein microarrays之操作原理，製作過程，以及應用範圍。課程中將生物晶片之種類與適用問題進行科學性、通俗性與系統性介紹，讓學生能夠有系統學習、易懂、並能實用。同時希望學生能藉由瞭解生物晶片及各式生醫系統之原理，引領學生對生物醫學檢測等基礎知識有所認知。並能啟發學生將來能協助生醫微製造技術(BioMEMS)的發展。因此課程設計上包括：1. 課程講授。2.學期末報告。另外上課以英文簡報介紹，培養學生未來以英文吸收專業知識之能力。

title: Neural Prostheses
description:
This class will introduce neural prostheses, neural stimulators, and modeling techniques for neural prostheses and neural stimulators. This class will also introduce neural response modeling techniques.
This course will cover the following topics:
(0) Introduction of the brain and the nervous system
(1) Neural implants and electronics.
(2) Introduction of neural prosthesis and neural stimulation device
- Cochlear implants, electrodes, signal processing, and programming
- Deep brain stimulation (DBS), DBS surgery, and programming
- Retinal implants
- BIONS (Bionic Neurons) implants
- Functional electrical stimulation
- Cuff electrodes, flat interface neural electrodes (FINE)
- Miscellaneous devices (if time permits)
(3) Introduction to computational neuroscience method
- RC circuits
- Cable model
- Hodgkin-Huxley model of action potential
- Activating functions
(4) Introduction to finite element method to study electric potential distribution in neurons & tissues
- 2D/3D models.
- Mesh generation.
- Material properties.
- Boundary conditions.
- Electrode-Tissue interface model
(5) Applications to electromagnetic, electric conduction, piezo-electric, thermal, and fluid flow problems (if time permits)
(6) Coupling problems (if time permits)
(7) Introduction to equivalent circuits (if time permits)
- Computation of equivalent resistors, capacitors, and inductors.
- Use of the SPICES program.
(8) Optimal design using genetic algorithms based on the finite element method and computational neuroscience techniques (if time permits).

title: Microcontrol techniques for neuroscience
description:
一、	課程目標
The goal of this course is to let student understand the current application of optogenetics, chemogenetic, magnetogenetic, sonogenetic and calcium imaging in neuroscience.
二、課程概述
This is an introductory level course of teaching optogenetics.
After this course, students will be able
1) to illustrate the current development of optogenetics, chemogenetics and magnetogenetics.
1) to read and analyze the calcium imaging technology
1) to criticize the current development of micro-control technology
這是一個關於光遺傳學的入門課程。學生可經由這堂課學習應用於神經科學的遺傳學基礎知識，包含光遺傳學、鈣離子攝影，以及其他使用遺傳學相關的神經科學技術

title: Introduction to Ultrasound and its Applications
description: This course will cover the physics of ultrasound and its biomedical applications. Starting from its generation and its propagation, the course will then examine various biomedical applications of ultrasound.

title: Modern Bioelectricity
description:
The classroom is changed to EF553A
This is an introductory course of electrophysiology. It covers the origin, propagation, measurement and analysis of bioelectricity based on an engineering quantitative framework, and briefly extends to clinical cardiac and neural electrophysiology. The aim is to provide engineering students with fundamental understanding of bioelectricty for future works.
本課程為電生理入門課程，以工程定量的觀念為基礎，涵蓋生物電的起源，傳導，量測與分析，並簡略延伸到臨床神經與心臟電生理診斷治療。目標在於建立理工背景學生從事跨領域生醫工程研究應用的電學基本知識。

title: Advanced of Biomedical Sensing and Old-age-medical
description:
This semester's courses will be taught online (09:30～12:00)
Link: https://meet.google.com/ppf-jaar-jyw
1. This course focuses on the comprehensive sensing principles, design and fabrication of medical sensors, and their various applications.

title: Digital Signal Processing
description: The fundamentals of discrete-time (digital) signal processing will be introduced in this course. Students will learn how to represent discrete-time signals and systems and analyze them using mathematical tools including discrete-time Fourier transform, z-transform, and discrete Fourier transform. Practical aspects such as structures or implementations for discrete-time systems, filter design methods, and fast Fourier transform will be also covered.

title: Machine Learning
Deep Learning
description: Deep learning is a branch of machine learning and recently receive a lot of attention due to its state-of-the art performance. Deep learning has been applied extensively to many areas such as computer vision, speech recognition, natural language processing, bioinformatics, and wireless networks. In this course, we will introduce various deep learning architectures and techniques, and discuss the advances in this area through paper presentation (by students). Students have the chance to practice implementing deep learning by doing programming homework and applying deep learning to real problems by doing final project.

title: Wireless Communications
description: This course provides the basic design and analysis of wireless communications systems. The topics range from wireless propagation channel, digital communication design and analysis, multiple access schemes, cell planning, MIMO, NOMA, etc. Students taking this course should especially learn (i) basic properties of wireless channels, such as fading and delay dispersion; (ii) basic digital communication for wireless systems, such as BER analysis in fading channels; (iii) methods that help dealing with wireless challenges, such as diversity; (iv) multi-user and multi-cell wireless systems; (v) advanced wireless techniques, such as MIMO and D2D communications; (vi) the ability to studying and investigating cutting-edge wireless communication systems, such as 5G and 6G systems.

title: Statistical Mechanics
description:
This course is quantum statistical mechanics.
Quantum Mechanics (535366) and Statistical Mechanics (535368) are combined classes to teach quantum physics.
As well-known, quantum physics is the basic scholar of modern science and technologies. It may be difficult for anyone to be a premier in nanotechnologies without the precise knowledge of quantum physics. However, what is  "quantum" appears quite strange to beginners. This class is then an introductory quantum physics for engineering students. In particular, we will hit what/how many guys misunderstand about quantum physics. For example, to solve Schrodinger equation differs from to know quantum physics. This just corresponds to the essence of quantum physics.  In quantum mechanics (535366), we will discuss mainly one quantum particle systems (ex., an electron). In Statistical Mechanics (535368), we will discuss many quantum particles system.
NOTE: strongly recommend to attend the Statistical Mechanics (535366), too.
I illustrate:
1) relationship between quantum mechanics and device engineering,
2) what the wavefunction is.
3) what to solve Schrodinger equation is.--- what the observation is.
4) several methods to solve Schrodinger equation.

title: Stochastic Processes
description: Teach students knowledge on stochastic processes and their applications in wireless communications and signal processing

title: VLSI System Design and Application
description: To establish students fundamental knowledge and skill  on VLSI.

title: Biomedical Engineering
description: The aim of this course is to study various research directions and areas related to biomedical engineering. We will utilize computer simulation tools or programming software, such as Python, to help us create models that may be useful to understand biomedical and biological phenomena.

title: Differential Equation
description: Differential equations are the language for quantitative sciences and engineering. In this course, we will discuss first order and higher order differential equations and their applications in solving practical problems. Specific techniques involving linear algebra, matrix arithmetic, Fourier series, and Laplace transform will be introduced toward this goal.

title: Probability
description: Teach the theory and applications of calculus-based probability theory. Applications of probability theory include but are not limited to wireless communication systems, computer networking, and machine learning.

title: Linear Algebra
description:
After the completion of this course, the students will be able to identify and solve systems involving linear equations, vector spaces, linear transformations, matrix representation of linear transformations, linear operators, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, similarity invariants and canonical forms. Applications to problems encountered electrical engineering will be given throughout the course.  Prerequisite: Basic algebra
Unlike previous years, the lecture this semester will be SUPPLEMENTED by video that are accessible from the course website.  Regular lectures will still be given in-class on Friday.  Assignments will be done in-class and in groups determined a priori to the first assignment.  The assignments will be done during Wednesday's lectures.

title: Signals and Systems
description: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the mathematical foundations of signals and systems. The course bridges theoretical abstractions with practical applications.

title: Electromagnetics
description:
Electromagnetic theory is the study of electric and magnetic fields and signals in space and time. It is essential to various applications in electrical engineering. This course will present a unified approach to electromagnetic theory based on postulates. The concept of fields (spatial distribution of physical quantities) and important mathematic tools are emphasized. Electrostatic and magnetostatic fields in space are then discussed. Time-varying fields, Maxwell’s equations, and concepts of electromagnetic waves will be introduced at the end of the semester.
This course will be divided into two modules and taught by two teachers respectively. All classes will have the same materials, schedules, and grading policy. Computer software (Matlab) may be utilized in the course to enhance the learning process.

title: Principles of Biomedical Engineering
description:
This course provides an introductory overview of the multi-disciplinary field of biomedical engineering. Biomedical engineers related to electrical engineering backgrounds need to understand the wide range of topics that are covered in this course, including anatomy and physiology, electrical engineering, biosignal processing and bioinstrumentation, biomechanics, biomaterials science and tissue engineering, radiation imaging medical imaging, and moral and ethical issues. It is intended to facilitate the student’s understanding in all areas of biomedical engineering so that they can appreciate the collaborative nature of the field.
Course Goals:
1.	Explore the introduction to and overview of the field of biomedical engineering.
2.	Understand the wide range of topics in biomedical engineering.

title: Discrete Mathematics
description:
Course Description:
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to Discrete Mathematics, the fundamental language of Computer Science and Information Engineering. Unlike Calculus, which deals with continuous data, Discrete Mathematics focuses on distinct, separable structures. The curriculum guides students through logic and proofs, induction, number theory, relations, graph theory, counting techniques, and finite automata. Students will learn to model real-world challenges using discrete mathematical structures and apply rigorous reasoning to solve computational problems.
Course Objectives:
1. Logical Rigor: To master logical reasoning and various proof techniques, including mathematical induction, as a basis for algorithmic thinking.
2. Structural Modeling: To understand and apply fundamental discrete structures such as sets, functions, and relations.
3. Number Theory: To explore the properties of integers and modular arithmetic, especially their applications in cryptography and network security.
4. Graph Theory: To analyze networks and trees, applying them to solve optimization and connectivity problems.
5. Combinatorics: To develop systematic counting skills for analyzing complexity and probability in discrete systems.
6. Theory of Computation: To introduce the basics of automata theory and deterministic finite state machines.

title: Introduction to VLSI Design
description:
This course aims to convey junior EE students techniques to analyze and design system by means of VLSI technology and CAD tools. Starting from VLSI process technology and transistor's behavior. an indepth discussion covering circuit, logic, and subsystem designs will be presented. Upon completion of the course, the student will be able to design system-level IC (SLIC) based on available VLSI technology and CAD tools. As such he/she will be able to work in a team of designers or stand alone to meet system-level specifications.
The course offers a complete yet accessible introduction to crosstalk models and optimization. It covers minimizing power consumption at every level of abstraction, from circuits to architecture and new insights into design-for-testability (DFT) techniques that maximize quality despite quicker turnarounds. It also presents detailed coverage of the algorithms underlying contemporary VLSI computer-aided design (CAD) software, so designers can understand their tools no matter which ones they choose. This course mainly contains 4 topics which are essential to the practice of VLSI design as a system design discipline. They are given below and will be addressed in more detail during lecture and discussion.
1. Transistor modeling and physical design constraints
2. Basic circuit and logic designs
3. Data path and sub-system designs
4. Design methodology for architecture optimization, testing and low-power

title: Introduction to Digital Communications
description: The primary objective of Introduction to Digital Communications is to provide students with a solid understanding of the fundamental principles that govern the operation and design of digital communication systems. By the end of the course, students are expected to comprehend the essential concepts underlying modern digital communication systems and standards. Furthermore, we aim for students to acquire the analytical and design skills necessary to evaluate and develop digital communication systems.

title: Theory and Modeling of   Semiconductor Nanostructures
description:
We are facing a big challenge in nanometer scale electronics. 1) Electron devices technologies are changing from FIN-FETs to NS-FETs. Hence, quantum mechanical effects are getting more notable in device physics, thanks to structural change as well as dimensional change. 2) The current basement of electronics is the drift-diffusion model that has been formulated assuming the PN junctions. Until when can we believe the drift-diffusion model? 3) New materials to be adopted in advanced transistors requires us to have more basic knowledge of material science. 4) Can Moore's law be continued?
We discuss those topics to compare them with the current technologies with sufficient reviews.

title: Data Science
description:
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to data science, covering:
•	Natural Language Processing (NLP): A review of the evolution of text processing, from linguistic fundamentals to modern language modeling.
•	Mathematical Foundations: A review of essential Probability and Linear Algebra required for understanding high-dimensional data and machine learning algorithms.
•	Learning with Graphs: Exploration of graph-based learning methods to identify patterns and perform predictive analysis on networked data.
•	Scalable Data Structures & Algorithms: Study of efficient data management through Hashing and the processing of Data Streams.
•	Practical Implementation: Hands-on experience through programming assignments that translate theoretical concepts into functional code.
•	Research Project: Development of professional research skills through a collaborative group project, learning a formal research presentation.

title: Governance and Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence
description: 本課程介紹人工智慧系統的治理架構與可信任設計原則，強調資料、模型與系統決策在不同階段對公平性、透明性、隱私與安全所造成的影響。課程內容包含人工智慧治理 (AI Governance)、責任導向設計、公平與偏誤分析、模型透明與可解釋性、隱私保護與系統安全等主題。學生將學習如何評估與設計具可信任特性的人工智慧系統，並透過實作深入理解技術選擇如何影響使用者信任與社會影響。

title: Medical Instrumentation: Application and Design
description:
This course introduces fundamental concepts applicable to biomedical instrumentation systems. Topics include the static and dynamic characteristics of measurement systems, the engineering design process, commercial development pathways, regulatory classifications, and electrical safety standards for medical devices.
The course emphasizes practical design principles, enabling students with limited electronics backgrounds to develop instruments that may not be commercially available. Students will learn the principles underlying various sensor mechanisms, analog signal processing (including amplifier and filter design), and digital data acquisition, processing, storage, and display using microcontrollers.
Applications covered include cardiovascular and respiratory measurements, biosensors, clinical laboratory instrumentation, medical imaging systems, as well as selected therapeutic and prosthetic devices.
Course Goals:
1.	Emphasize engineering design principles to enable students to develop medical instrumentation systems.
2.	Provide updated coverage of modern sensor technologies and signal processing techniques.
3.	Introduce contemporary microcontroller applications in biomedical instrumentation.
4.	Present revised and updated chapters, descriptions, and references reflecting current advancements.
5.	Strengthen analytical and problem-solving skills through comprehensive worked examples.
6.	Provide supplementary learning materials via a companion webpage.
7.	Offer a solutions manual containing complete solutions to all problems for instructional support.

title: Geometrical Optics
description: The aim of this course is to provide the basics of the geometrical optics and understand the role of geometrical optics in optical instruments and physical system. The first half of the course is mainly to cover the fundamental concept of the geometrical optics and its applications to some simple optical instruments, such as lenses and mirrors. The second half of the course focuses on the ray equations and the applications to more advanced optical instruments.

title: The Optical Properties of Materials
description: This class aims to discuss the optical properties of materials. The class starts from the classical description of optical transmission and reflection followed by the quantum mechanical description of optical absorption and emission in materials and effect of excitons. The materials mentioned throughout this class include semiconductors, metals, low dimensional material and organic materials. Therefore, the objective of this class is to teach student to understand the classical treatment of optical propagation in the solid materials, quantum mechanical treatment of absorption and emission in materials, the importance of the exciton in the materials, and the origin of the optical nonlinear effect in the crystals.

title: Intro.to Quantum Optics
description:
量子物理的發展已在許多領域展現巨大潛力，近年來這股發展正全面地改變許多現有的科技，並且進而影響甚至預期主導產業的革命，世界上無論是大公司或是新創都積極參與其中。在這堂課中，我們介紹量子光學的理論基礎，讓學生可以瞭解與參與這方面的研究與最新的發展如 quantum communication, quantum sensing and imaging, photonic qubits, quantum computation, and so on.
1.	Introduce the quantum theory of lights and light-matter interaction.
2.	Introduce math and physics needed to begin research in quantum optics
3.     Discuss current researches and technologies using quantum optics
Objectives:
a. To describe the quantum properties of light and to identify differences between classical and quantum light
b. To know and be able to calculate quantities that measure the quantum extent
c. To know the advantages of quantum optics and the potential applications
d. To explore recent researches in quantum optics

title: Modern Methods of Optical Spectroscopy
description:
Spectroscopy, the measurement of the interaction between light and matter, has played an essential role in wild applications in our daily lives. Advances in this field have contributed to the development of lasers, gas sensing, single-molecule sensors, telescopes for exoplanet discovery, medical devices, etc. Further, taking advantage of newly developed photonics, some modern methods of optical spectroscopy have led to major breakthroughs in atmospheric science, remote sensing, instrument miniaturization, and Mars explorations. In each topic of this course, besides theoretical concepts and experimental techniques, we will also discuss interesting applications.
At the end of this course, students will be expected to have a basic knowledge of this field, ideas about how most spectroscopy instruments work, and knowledge of how to read a paper. Also, I hope this class will bring together students from a variety of interests or probably different backgrounds, and we will practice communicating across disciplines based on our understanding of optical spectroscopy.
This course will encourage students to use AI and practice critical thinking. With AI support, students will work on finding the best solution or the most convincing explanation.https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vZ1kAuU_ogw

title: Semiconductor Physics and Devices (I)
description:
Semiconductor technology is at the heart of every advanced electronic system—smartphones, 5G infrastructure, AI accelerators, cloud computing, electric vehicles, and beyond. As these applications surge, the demand for innovative semiconductor devices and materials has never been higher.
This course provides a foundational yet forward-looking introduction to Semiconductor Physics and Devices, the core knowledge required for researchers and engineers in the Semiconductor, IC, optoelectronics, and power electronics industries.
半導體技術是所有先進電子系統的核心——從智慧型手機、5G 基礎建設、AI 加速器、雲端運算到電動車，都不可或缺。隨著這些應用快速成長，對創新半導體元件與材料的需求也達到前所未有的高度。
本課程將從基礎到前瞻，帶來「半導體物理與元件」的完整介紹，這是所有從事半導體、積體電路、光電、電力電子等領域的研究者與工程師必備的核心知識。
We will cover:
1. Fundamental semiconductor material properties
2. Carrier transport: drift, diffusion, and recombination
3. Operating principles of key devices: p–n diode, BJT, MOSFET, FinFET, GAA, and CFET.
4. Emerging challenges in device scaling (short-channel effects, ultra-thin dielectrics, SS limits)
5. A forward look into beyond-Moore technologies, including new materials, architectures, and device concepts
By combining rigorous physics with real-world examples and the latest industry trends, the course prepares students for careers in semiconductor R&D, IC design, reliability engineering, and advanced manufacturing.
課程內容涵蓋：
1. 半導體材料的基本特性
2. 載子傳輸機制：漂移、擴散與復合
3. 重要元件的操作原理：p–n 接面二極體、BJT、MOSFET、FinFET、GAA and CFET.
4. 元件微縮時所面臨的新挑戰：短通道效應、超薄介電層、次臨界擺幅限制等
5. 超越摩爾定律的前瞻技術，包括新材料、新架構與創新元件概念
本課程透過嚴謹的物理推導、實例分析與產業最新趨勢，協助學生建立扎實的半導體基礎，並為未來在半導體研發、IC 設計、可靠度工程及先進製造領域的職涯發展做好準備。
Intended Learning Outcomes (ILOs)（預期學習成果）
By the end of the course, you will be able to:
1. Explain the essential semiconductor material properties and device physics.
2. Analyze the operating principles of p–n diodes, MOSFETs, BJTs, FinFET, GAA and CFET using physical models.
3. Evaluate modern scaling challenges—short-channel effects, ultra-thin dielectrics, subthreshold swing limits—and identify the underlying device-physics problems.
4. Propose innovative device structures or design strategies to address limitations in next-generation semiconductor technologies.
-Innovation begins with understanding and solving the right problems.
預期學期成果:
在本課程結束時，修課的學生能夠：
1.解釋半導體材料特性及元件物理
2.利用元件物理分析半導體原件操作原理。
3.評估在微縮下半導體元件的議題，包含短通道效應、超薄介電層及次臨界擺伏限制。
4.提出元件設計來克服半導體元件發展的挑戰。

title: Intelligent Fog Computing Systems and Designs
Optimization Theory and Applications
description:
This course will focus on convex optimization, which has been used in efficiently solving many signal processing and communications problems, thanks to the development of interior point method (IPM), specifically the primal-dual IP algorithm.  The course will include both 1) problem modeling (formulation), i.e. recognizing if a problem is convex, and if possible, turning a seemingly nonconvex problem into a convex one, and 2) learning the algorithms, mainly the IPM and its variations, that can efficiently solve the problem.  Due to the large amount of content we need to cover, some of the materials will be taught offline via video.
We will NOT be covering integer nor mixed-integer convex programming, nor problems that involve nondifferentiable functions, which may require the use of subgradient and subgradient methods.  However, individual discussions can be held based on the student's research needs.
Unlike previous years, the lecture this semester will be SUPPLEMENTED by video that are accessible from the course website.  Regular lectures will still be given in-class on Friday.  Assignments will be done in-class and in groups determined a priori to the first assignment.  The assignments will be done during Wednesday's lectures.

title: Detection and Estimation
description: This is considered a fundamental course in statistical signal processing. Topics that will be covered will include classical and Bayesian estimation. Hypothesis testing: Neyman-Pearson Theorem, Bayesian Approach  and GLRT (if possible).

title: Bio-Medical Circuits and Systems
description:
This graduate-level course is focused on the emerging biomedical electronics which should create innovative solutions for today's health problems and pose new challenges for the Electronics Engineering community to build new bridges at the frontiers of Biomedical Engineering.
This course is for students who wish to familiarize themselves with biomedical electronics and may commit to go on to do biomedical electronics and instrumentations research, or to work in the biomedical electronics industry.

title: Integrated Circuit Design Laboratory
description:
This course aims to convey the senior and graudated EE students techniques to design the VLSI chips using state-of-the-art CAD tools. In addition to learning CAD tools for performance-driven and cost-effective IC designs, a top-down design flow and related environment will also be addressed. Upon completion of the course, the student will be able to design the integrated circuits and systems based on standard cell library as well as full-custom layout approaches. As such he/she will be able to work in a team of designers or stand alone.
The course starts from system design specs of an application which demands the need of developing specific hardwares or application specific integrated circuits (ASIC) or application processors. Then followed by the presentation of architectural proposals, an optimal architecture leading to performance-driven and cost-effective realization can be derived based on both sampling rate and system clock rate. With the support of Verilog-HDL, designers can describe their designs either in behavioral level or structural level. Before going down to the lower level design, one has to do initial floorplan to estimate both routing style and module aspect ratio which provide some area constraints for later designs. Then the partitioned blocks can be conducted hierarchically and with the support of synthesis as well as P&R routing tools, physical layout can easily be achieved if cell-based design approach is exploited. Finally through layout verification and post-layout simulation, the design can be verified before fabrication.

title: Computer Architecture
description:
(Classroom is changed to EDB13) (教室改到工四館地下一樓合勤講堂)

This course is intended to give students a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental architecture of modern computing systems. Students will learn the structure of basic modules in a computer, and how they interact with each other. Design trade-offs, performance evaluation, and future trend of modern computing systems will also be discussed.

title: Silicon photonics
description:
課程時間: M567
Silicon photonics is an innovative field that merges photonics and electronics to manipulate light on a photonic chip. By leveraging silicon's optical properties, this technology enables the integration of optical components like waveguides, modulators, and detectors directly onto silicon chips. This integration facilitates faster data transmission and processing speeds, lower power consumption, and compact device designs.  This course aims to provide students with a fundamental understanding of silicon photonics, covering key topics such as applications, device properties, and fabrication processes. Students will also gain practical experience by realizing the optical functionalities of waveguides through numerical simulations.

title: Machine Learning Intelligent Chip Design
description:
機器學習晶片在近年來被廣泛的應用於各式邊緣運算的應用中，機器學習晶片屬於多核心系統晶片設計的一個分支，本課程使用SystemC語言讓學生了解一個多核心系統晶片設計架構的評估與運作方式。首先將介紹機器學習晶片的設計概論，接著介紹脈動陣列(systolic array)以及晶片內網路架構。最後，本課程也將介紹多核心系統晶片的架構以及運作流程，使學生能了解一個機器學習系統晶片設計的完整運作方式，並有能力透過SytemC語言來實現。
The machine learning chip has been widely applied to various applications of edge computing in recent years. It is a branch of the multi-processor system on chip (MPSoC). This course will enable students to use SystemC to understand and evaluate the operational mechanisms of MPSoC.  Initially, the course will cover the fundamentals of machine learning chip design methods. Following this, it will introduce the systolic array architecture and the Network-on-Chip (NoC) architecture. Finally, the course will explore MPSoC architecture and its operational flow, with the goal of helping students comprehend the complete operational mechanism of Machine Learning MPSoC and implement it using SystemC.

title: Reliability and Failure Physics of Semiconductor Devices
description:
"Reliability is, after all, engineering in its most practical form" said by James R. Schlesinger - Former US Secretary of State for Defense. Reliability is an essential part of a successful semiconductor product because it is related to trust. No reliability is equal to no business. Especially, the new technologies based on the advanced designs and novel materials, e.g., FinFETs, high k dielectrics, wide bandgap, Ferroelectric, or 2D materials, cannot be commercialized without the proven reliability. Therefore, a good R&D engineer should recognize the statistical tools/characterization methods, identify the reliability issues,and evaluate failure physics, further designing for reliability. In this course, the basic semiconductor devices/processes, statistical tools, and characterization methods for reliability evaluation are covered. Furthermore, four most important main reliability challenges (Bias temperature instability & interface traps / Time dependent dielectric breakdown / Mass transport-induced failures / Electrostatic discharge (ESD)) will be addressed in this class.
前美國國防部部長 James R. Schlesinger曾說：可靠度是工程中最實際的層面。高可靠度是所有半導體產品成功的重要因素，因為可靠度與客戶對產品的信任有關。沒有可靠度等於沒有客戶的信賴而失去商業價值。對先進的半導體技術，例如FinFET、高介電常數絕緣層、寬能隙、鐵電或二維材料等，如果無法通過可靠度驗證，這些技術將無法商品化。因此，優秀的研發工程師應該具備評估可靠度所需統計工具/量測方法來確定可靠度問題，並評估特性衰退的物理特性，並進一步設計高可靠度產品。本課程中將深入淺出的介紹基本半導體元件/製程及可靠度評估所需的統計工具和量測方法。此外，本課程也將會探討四個最重要也最常見的半導體元件可靠度議題（偏壓溫度不穩定性和界面缺陷 Bias temperature instability & interface traps / 依時性閘極崩潰 Time dependent dielectric breakdown / 質量傳輸引起的故障 Mass transport-induced failures / 靜電放電 ESD）。
Intended Learning Outcomes (ILOs):
By the end of this class, you should be able to:
1. Explain the basic operation principles and fabrication processes for the MOS type semiconductor technologies
2. Apply the basic statistics/statistical tools for reliability analysis
3. Evaluate the failure physics of reliability issues
4. Present the reliability issues using your own word
5. Design for reliability (DFR)
預期學習成果：
在本課程結束時，修課的學生能夠：
1.解釋MOS半導體技術的基本工作原理和製程
2.應用基本的統計工具進行可靠度分析
3.評估導致不穩定元件特性的失效物理機制
4.闡述對可靠度問題的見解
5.增強可靠度的元件設計（Design for reliability）

title: Memory Circuits and System
description: The goal of this course aims to learn the fundamental memory circuits and to gain the basic understanding of hierarchy memory system design methodology. The first part of the course focuses on the embedded-memory circuit design from latches, register file, SRAM, CAM to embedded DRAM and embedded non-volatile memory. We then discuss the design challenges and techniques of high-performance SRAM in nanoscale CMOS technologies. The impacts of technology scaling, such as signal loss due to leakage and degradation of noise margin due to Vt scatter are addressed. Design directions and leakage/variation/degradation tolerant SRAM circuit techniques to mitigate various performance and reliability constraints are discussed and examples are given and merits discussed. Alternative cell structures for low-voltage SRAM. Some design issues and opportunities in advanced technologies are illustrated. The second part of the course covers the basics of DRAM and embedded NVRAM. It is intended to introduce the students to the basic idea, cell structure, and sensing schemes of these memories. The third part of this course is to discuss the hierarchy memory system from the aspect of applications, including memory interface, 3D memory, memory coherence and computation-in-memory.

description:
This course aims to provide students with an in-depth understanding of the fundamental concepts and techniques in computer vision, including image formation, image feature extraction, 3D reconstruction, image segmentation, object recognition, deep learning, object detection, object tracking, and face recognition. Students will also gain proficiency in implementing and applying algorithms, models, and frameworks related to computer vision, equipping them to solve computer vision problems in various fields such as autonomous driving, smart homes, and medical image analysis.
In addition, the course features a special joint lecture by Dr. Chia-Ming Cheng (鄭嘉珉) from MediaTek’s AI Technology Division, who will share the latest industry insights and perspectives, offering students an in-depth exploration of real-world challenges and business opportunities in both research and end-product applications of computer vision.
Through this course, students will understand the limitations and challenges of existing computer vision applications and explore future development directions. By the end of the course, students will have developed the following abilities:
	Students will possess basic knowledge and technical skills in computer vision and image processing.
	Students will have sensitivity to emerging technologies and trends, along with strong analytical abilities.

title: Memory Device and Process Technology
description:
課程概述：半導體記憶體是現代積體電路中的核心元件，廣泛應用於電腦系統與各類電子產品中。根據資料儲存特性，記憶體可分為揮發性記憶體（Volatile Memory）與非揮發性記憶體（Non-Volatile Memory）。
揮發性記憶體如靜態隨機存取記憶體（Static Random Access Memory, SRAM）與動態隨機存取記憶體（Dynamic Random Access Memory, DRAM），主要用於資料暫存，在系統運行中提供高效能的即時存取功能。而非揮發性記憶體則能在無電源供應的情況下，長期保存資料，這得益於其特殊的半導體元件與物理機制（如快閃記憶體中浮動閘極的電荷儲存）。常見的非揮發性記憶體包括記憶卡、隨身碟、快閃記憶體（Flash Memory）及唯讀記憶體（Read-Only Memory, ROM）等。
本課程將詳細介紹揮發性記憶體中的 SRAM 與 DRAM，以及非揮發性記憶體中的 ROM 與 Flash，重點涵蓋其操作原理、基本記憶單元結構與製造技術、感應放大器設計、陣列架構、製程技術與挑戰等。同時，課程將介紹前瞻性記憶體技術（如相變記憶體 PCM、阻變記憶體 RRAM、自旋轉移矩磁性記憶體 MRAM、鐵電記憶體 FeRAM 等），並對其操作原理、特性、結構及潛在應用進行深入探討與評估。
目標：本課程旨在幫助學生掌握當前與未來記憶體元件的應用與技術發展，通過回顧記憶體技術的演進歷程與微縮挑戰，引導學生深入了解各種新興記憶體技術的基礎原理、結構設計、製程技術、優缺點以及當前的研究熱點。本課程適合對固態記憶體元件發展趨勢感興趣的學生選修，特別是已具備半導體元件物理與工程基礎的研究生或大四學生。

title: Vector Calculus
description:
In this course we introduce vector field and consider the integral theorems in 2 and 3 dimensions.
The goal of this course is to make a strong connection from calculus to other analysis courses.

title: Fundamental Graph Theory
description: This is an introductory course on graph theory. Basic concepts, essential topics and theorems, and applications in other areas (including optimization) will be discussed. Students are expected to build a foundational understanding of graph theory, and learn how to model and solve problems from other subjects using it.

title: Introduction to Real Analysis
description:
This course provides an introduction to measure theory and Lebesgue integration, with emphasis on both the concrete theory on Euclidean spaces and the abstract theory of measure spaces. Topics include Lebesgue measure, measurable functions, the Lebesgue integral, convergence theorems, abstract measure spaces, modes of convergence, product measures, and the Fubini-Tonelli theorem. Selected topics in differentiation theory may also be covered as time permits.
The main objectives are to develop a rigorous understanding of measure and integration, to learn the standard tools of modern real analysis, and to prepare students for further study in analysis, partial differential equations, probability, and functional analysis.

title: Introduction to Combinatorics
description: This is an introductory course on graduate level combinatorics, which is a required course of the Combinatorics Graduate Program and includes half of the syllabus of the Ph.D. qualification exam of Combinatorics (the other half will be from "Graph Theory"). Topics include enumerative combinatorics, extremal combinatorics, and several fundamental combinatorial structures. If times permits, methods from other areas such as probability, (linear) algebra, and discrete geometry/topology are also discussed.

title: Stochastic Processes
description: Stochastic processes will broadly appear in a part of science, finance and social studies. The aim of this course is to understand stochastic process from the theoretical point of view and be familiar with how to handle it at the basic level. The course will be considered as an application of Probability Theory and Advanced Probability Theory. Thus we assume that students have been already familiar with measure-theory based probability theory.

title: Topics in Discrete Maths.
description: The aim of this course is to improve students' English reading ability and develop students' English presentation skills.

title: Degenerate elliptic and parabolic PDEs
description: The goal of the class is to become familiar with some of the theory related to degenerate nonlinear elliptic and parabolic PDEs. We will focus on the p-Laplacian in the elliptic case, and on the porous medium equation in the parabolic case.

title: Python and Machine Learning Algorithms
description: Machine learning has been shown powerful on many specific problems. While there are many existing packages to perform various machine learning tasks, we must understand the relations between the parameters and the outcome. This course will start with an overview of linear algebra, which is the foundation of many machine learning algorithms. Then you will learn the theory behind each algorithm and how to implement them from scratch (which should be fun!). With these insights, you will be more confident in picking the models, tuning the hyperparameters, and even contriving new algorithms.

title: CAD/CAM Theories and Practices
description:
This course aims to develop students’ integrated capabilities in computer-aided design and manufacturing (CAD/CAM) through English-medium instruction, project-based learning (PBL), case analysis, technical discussion, hands-on practice, and research-oriented training. No prior advanced CAD/CAM or research experience is required. The course is scaffolded from fundamental modeling and manufacturing concepts toward parametric design, mechanism analysis, CAM planning, prototype development, experimental validation, and research communication.
Students will learn to analyze world-class engineering and product design cases, identify their underlying engineering principles, limitations, and innovation opportunities, and transform these observations into researchable engineering questions. The course also introduces literature search strategies, journal quality assessment, research gap identification, and evidence-based technical discussion.
The course does not require a specific CAD/CAM software platform. Selected tools will be demonstrated in class, while students may adopt appropriate software according to project needs. By the end of the course, students are expected to complete a research-oriented PBL project integrating design, analysis, manufacturing, validation, and technical presentation. High-quality projects may be further developed toward journal publication.
Week 1 — Course Introduction: From Zero to Research-Ready
Week 2 — Global Design Benchmarking and Engineering Observation
Week 3 — Literature Search, Journal Selection, and Research Landscape
Week 4 — From Design Case to Research Question
Week 5 — Parametric CAD and Design Variables
Week 6 — Advanced Modeling, Assembly, and Mechanism Design
Week 7 — Simulation, Research Methodology, and Validation Strategy
Week 8 — Research Proposal and Design Review I
Week 9 — Design Optimization and DFMA
Week 10 — CAM Fundamentals and Process Planning
Week 11 — Toolpath Generation and Manufacturing Simulation
Week 12 — Prototype Manufacturing and Assembly
Week 13 — Measurement, Metrology, and Experimental Data Collection
Week 14 — Data Analysis and Digital–Physical Validation
Week 15 — Research Discussion, Contribution, and Paper-Oriented Reporting
Week 16 — Final Research Defense and Prototype Demonstration

title: Servo Control
description:
This course aims to guide graduate students in a deep dive into the control technologies of advanced power converters and electric motor drives, laying a solid foundation for their master's thesis research. The course uses Jose Rodriguez's classic work, *Predictive Control of Power Converters and Electrical Drives* (Wiley, 2012), as the core textbook, and incorporates international journal articles to guide students across theoretical foundations and connect them with cutting-edge international research.
This course fully adopts the flipped classroom model, cultivating students' independent reading, logical reasoning, and academic presentation skills. Students are required to give weekly presentations on key technologies in electric motor servo control, with a particular focus on the theoretical innovation and practical applications of predictive current control. Discussion topics cover finite-state model predictive control, cost function design, simulation, and multi-stage converter integration. The ultimate goal of this course is to help students identify and establish their master's thesis research direction. Through weekly analysis of cutting-edge papers and peer discussions, students can accurately grasp the technological bottlenecks in academia and industry, develop the ability to appreciate international journal articles, possess strong academic expression skills, and cultivate innovative thinking abilities, thereby enabling them to develop forward-looking research.
W1: Introduction
W2-W16: Reports + Lectures on International Journal Articles
Midterm Exam Week: Reports
Final Exam Week: Reports

title: Intelligent Control Systems
description:
This course introduces intelligent control systems, from algorithms to mechanisms, through theory, practical implementation, and publication. Students study systems that perceive, learn, make inferences, and optimize their behavior using incomplete information and under uncertainty.
Theory focuses on three principles of soft computing and artificial intelligence: inference through fuzzy logic for decision-making, learning through neural networks for modeling and error reduction, and evolution through genetic algorithms for optimization and adaptation.
Practical work combines simulation with implementation on aerial, ground, surface, and underwater mobile robots. Problem-based Learning (PbBL) and Project-based Learning (PjBL) develop teamwork through in-class tasks, a concept-generation proposal, and a proof-of-concept project. Publication training develops English academic writing using IEEE paper style.

title: Spectrometer Optical System – Design Principles and Applications
description:
本課程旨在深入探討光譜儀的工作原理與其光學設計的基本理論，並延伸到光譜學分析在產業中的實際應用，讓學生能全面理解光譜儀從物理基礎理論到實際應用的完整過程。除此之外還有實作部分，讓學生有機會參與光譜檢測系統的設計、組裝、控制等應用開發。透過實踐活動，鞏固理論知識、提高實際問題解決能力。
本課程將帶領學生深入了解光譜儀的原理及應用，首先從光譜學的基本概念開始，探討原子光譜成因以及光柵繞射分光的基礎理論，建立學生在光學領域的知識基礎。隨後，課程將轉入光學設計原理，包括聚焦系統與光路設計關鍵要素，使學生能夠理解並設計出有效的光譜儀光學系統。在介紹光譜儀應用部分，將探討UV光譜儀、VIS-NIR光譜儀以及NIR光譜儀等不同型態的操作原理與實際案例，並深入光譜儀在生化檢驗或工業4.0監控場域中的關鍵應用。此外，課程將重點介紹如何利用微型控制器（如Python編程環境下的Raspberry Pi）進行系統整合，培養學生在實際情境中解決問題的能力。最終，在實作環節，學生將進行如水質檢測與顏色辨識等專題項目，這不僅將理論與實踐相結合，也將進一步鞏固學生的專業技能，為日後在科研或產業界的發展奠定基礎。

title: Calculus (I)
description:
微積分是現代科學、工程及人工智慧等領域的重要數學基礎，廣泛應用於各種科學與工程問題。本課程為期一年，將介紹微積分的基本概念與方法，包括極限、微分、積分及偏微分等內容。透過理論講解與實際應用，培養學生理解與運用微積分的基本能力，為未來進階課程及專業領域的學習奠定良好的數學基礎。
Calculus is a fundamental mathematical foundation for modern science, engineering, artificial intelligence, and many other disciplines. It provides essential tools for analyzing and solving a wide range of scientific and engineering problems. This one-year course introduces the fundamental concepts and methods of calculus, including limits, differentiation, integration, and partial differentiation. Through theoretical instruction and practical applications, students will develop essential skills in understanding and applying calculus, providing a solid mathematical foundation for advanced coursework and professional studies.
In this course, I will introduce recent applications of calculus in advanced AI research. Rather than introducing mathematical concepts only from a theoretical perspective, I will first present practical applications to help students understand why these mathematical methods are important and how they are used in real-world AI research.
We will then explore the corresponding concepts and methods in the textbook, followed by a return to the original AI applications. This application–theory–application approach is designed to help students connect mathematical concepts with their practical use and develop a deeper understanding of the subject.
In the TA sessions, we will focus on hands-on calculations and problem-solving. TAs will provide step-by-step explanations of selected textbook exercises and guide students through the calculation process. Through repeated practice, students will become familiar with fundamental calculation techniques and develop the computational skills necessary to apply calculus confidently to problems within each topic.
Topics
1. Functions (Chapter 1)
2. Limits and Continuity (Chapter 2)
3. Derivatives (Chapter 3)
4. Applications of Derivatives (Chapter 4)
5. Integrals (Chapter 5)
6. Applications of Definite Integrals (Chapter 6)
7. Inverse Functions (Chapter 7)

In particular, we cover some theoretical treatment like fundamental theorem of calculus, mean value theorem, chain rule, l'Hopital rule, integration by parts, to name a few. Some other topics like infinite sequences and series, partial derivatives, and multiple integrals will also be discussed, for at least the introductory items. After all, some applications of calculus in science and engineering will be studied too from time to time to build solid learning experience for students.

title: Embedded System Design
description:
This hands-on course introduces students to embedded systems, IoT, TinyML, Edge AI, and AI-powered applications through practical, project-based learning. Students will work with the Wio Terminal(Arduino), sensors, actuators, and cloud services to build interactive embedded systems and connected IoT applications.
The course progressively introduces machine learning on embedded devices, including TinyML and Edge Impulse for sensor-based gesture recognition, object detection, sound and motion classification, and anomaly detection. Students will also explore IoT development with Blynk, computer vision with MediaPipe, and AI-assisted application development using NVIDIA DLI and large language models.
Rather than focusing only on individual programming exercises, the course emphasizes integrating hardware, software, data, and AI into functional prototypes. Students will work in small teams to develop their own projects, collect and process real-world data, train and deploy AI models, and demonstrate the resulting systems through a midterm prototype and a final project.
By the end of the course, students will have practical experience designing and implementing AI-enabled embedded systems, from sensor data acquisition and embedded programming to machine learning inference, IoT connectivity, and interactive AI applications.

title: Advanced Modern Networking
description:
Recent advances in virtualization technologies are revolutionizing the IT and telecommunications landscapes accelerating their convergence. This course will cover the evolution of computing and networking platforms, with emphasis on the requirements of a service provider. Specific attention will be devoted to Data Center architectures and the concept of virtualization (processing, storage, networking aspects). The course will then address the latest advances and research challenges in Software Defined Networking and Network Function Virtualization concepts and their impact on the design, deployment, and management of ICT services. The course will also address various distributed cloud architectures such as edge and fog computing and research challenges.

title: Cybersecurity Threat Analysis and Secure AI
description:
本課程將介紹惡意威脅分析，並以此來探討AI Security(人工智慧安全)領域的兩個面向: “AI for Cybersecurity” (如何利用AI系統來解決資安問題)，以及“Cybersecurity for AI” (AI系統自身存在的資安漏洞)。前者包括AI技術如何應用於惡意威脅偵測等資安議題；後者包括AI系統本身存在的資料隱私安全問題、對抗式攻擊問題、分散式AI計算環境的資安問題等等。最後將結合以上兩者說明如何建構具有安全人工智慧的惡意威脅分析系統。
This course will introduce threat analysis and use it to explore two aspects of AI Security: "AI for Cybersecurity" (how AI systems can be used to address cybersecurity issues), and "Cybersecurity for AI" (the security vulnerabilities inherent in AI systems themselves). The former includes how AI technology can be applied to cybersecurity issues such as malicious threat detection; the latter covers issues such as data privacy security in AI systems, adversarial attacks, and cybersecurity in distributed AI computing environments. Finally, we will integrate the above two aspects to explain how to construct a threat analysis system with secure AI.

title: Calculus (II)
description:
Calculus is a fundamental course for engineering students. It plays an important role in the understanding of science, engineering, economics, and computer science. Calculus (II) will cover the following topics. The first topic is about how to model the motion of an object by the parametric equations of its position together with how to calculate the derivative and arc length of the corresponding plane curve. Subsequently, the parametric equations of position are transformed into the form of vector-valued function of position such that the velocity and the acceleration can be easily represented by the first and the second derivative in vector form. Second, we will extend the concept of differentiation (i.e., slope) to multi-variable function with respect to each independent variable. This is referred to as the partial derivative, which corresponds to the gradient vector. Gradient vector can be further applied to iteratively optimize the function and has been extensively used for model training in deep-learning applications. The integration of multi-variable function can also be used to estimate the volume under a 2D surface and the moment of mass for a 3D object. Third, the concept of vector field will be introduced. Then, the work done by the vector field on a moving object can be estimated using line integral. Similarly, it is also possible to calculate the flux through a surface or a contour by flux integral in the vector field.
CH 8   Parametric equations and Polar coordinate (參數方程式與極座標)
CH 9   Vectors and Geometry of space (空間向量與空間座標)
CH 10  Vector-valued functions (空間向量函數)
CH 11  Functions of several variables (多變數函數與其導數)
CH 12  Multiple integral (多重積分)
CH 13  Vector analysis (向量分析: 線積分與面積分)

Vector Analysis
The Vector Analysis course aims to help students understand and apply vector concepts in multivariable calculus. This course primarily covers fundamental theories such as vector fields, line integrals, surface integrals, gradients, divergences, and curls. Through examples, students will deepen their understanding of vector operations in physical phenomena. Ultimately, students should be able to apply these mathematical tools to the field of electrical engineering.
Complex Variables
The Complex Variables course is designed to guide students in gaining a deep understanding of complex number theory and its applications in analysis. The course covers essential concepts such as the basic properties of complex numbers, analytic functions, Cauchy's theorem, and the residue theorem, and applies these theories to problems in physics and engineering. By the end of the course, students should be proficient in the techniques of complex analysis and be able to apply them to solve various complex number-related problems.
This course provides students with a powerful set of mathematical tools, enabling them to gain a deeper understanding and analysis of various phenomena in nature.
The main course content is outlined as follows.
1. Vector functions, gradient field and directional derivatives
2. Divergence and Curl
3. Line integral
4. Surface integral
5. Complex numbers and Complex functions
6. Integration in the complex plane
7. Complex sequences and Series - Taylor and Laurent expansions
8. Singularities and the Residue theorem

title: Probability
description:
This course begins by introducing probability models and their applications in the fields of electrical engineering and computer science. Next, we will cover the fundamental concepts of probability, including probability axioms, counting methods, conditional probability, independent events, and sequential experiments. We will then introduce the concept of random variables, exploring cumulative distribution functions (CDFs), probability density functions (PDFs), functions of random variables, expected values, Markov’s inequality, and various transforms. Subsequently, the course will extend the discussion of a single random variable to multiple random variables. Finally, we will investigate the properties of the sum of multiple random variables, introducing the sample mean, the Law of Large Numbers, and the Central Limit Theorem.
1. Probability Models

3. Counting Methods
4. Conditional Probability
5. Independence

8. Functions of Random Variable
9. Transform Methods
10. Sums of Random Variables

The demand for power supply quality from all sectors is increasingly urgent, making it necessary to assess the insulation status of various electrical equipment in advance. Among the various diagnostic methods, the identification of partial discharge is particularly promising. This course first explores the causes and related theories of partial discharge occurring in gas, liquid, and solid insulating materials. Secondly, it elaborates on the relevant detection frameworks and standards and discusses various analytical methods for processing measurement data. Furthermore, it examines graphical identification techniques for evaluating insulation status. Finally, the course applies these various techniques to several electrical devices and provides examples to illustrate the importance of partial discharge. The course will primarily be conducted through lectures, supplemented by interactive discussions.
1. The theories of partial discharges in gas, liguid, and solid.

title: Nonlinear Programming
description:
Optimization is central to any problem involving decision making, whether in engineering or in economics. The task of decision making entails choosing between various alternatives. This choice is governed by our desire to make the “best” decision. The measure of goodness of the alternatives is described by an objective function or performance index. Optimization theory and methods deal with selecting the best alternative in the sense of the given objective function. The purpose of this course is to provide a working knowledge of optimization theory and methods. To accomplish this goal, we include many examples that illustrate the theory and algorithms discussed in the class. However, it is not my intention to provide a cookbook of the most recent numerical techniques for optimization; rather, my goal is to equip the students with sufficient background for further study of advanced topics in optimization.
最佳化是在很多領域中常面對的問題，在決策過程中當面對不同可選擇的可能中，如何選擇最好的是最佳化所要解決的。在這門課中，我們將介紹相關的最佳化理論及方法。基本上，去提供所有的常用可能的最佳化數值技術是不可能，因此，本課程主要在於提供學生充分之知識與概念，以足於當面對任何最佳化問題時知道如何解決。
Tentative Outline
	Introduction of Optimization Problems
	One-Dimensional Search
	Gradient Methods
	Newton’s Method and Its Variations
	The Use of Computational Intelligence
	Linear Programming
	Nonlinear Constrained Optimization

title: Machine Learning Techniques and Applications
description:
This course equips senior undergraduate and graduate students with fundamental machine learning knowledge and practical model-investigation skills using guided learning activities. Topics include classification, regression, clustering, dimensionality reduction, feature extraction, model evaluation, and introductory deep learning and reinforcement learning. Students are expected to explain modeling choices, interpret validation evidence, identify limitations, compare alternative approaches, and defend conclusions. As an EMI course, students will develop the ability to communicate technical ideas and experimental evidence in English through team investigations, peer questioning, Padlet-based evidence sharing, and oral defense. The four core competencies are Explain, Defend, Critique, and Reflect.
The course begins with the machine learning workflow, including data, features, labels, training, validation, testing, and model evaluation. Students then study major classification methods, including kNN, Naïve Bayes, discriminant analysis, decision trees, SVMs, ensemble methods, and neural networks. Regression topics include linear, robust and regularized regression, support vector regression, regression trees, ensembles, Gaussian processes, and neural networks. The course further covers clustering methods, dimensionality reduction, feature selection, and feature extraction from raw and time-varying signals. Deep learning is introduced through neural representations, transfer learning, training curves, and model limitations. The semester concludes with an evidence-based team symposium and an industry expert workshop on reinforcement learning, while class activities emphasize controlled comparison, evidence interpretation, peer questioning, and English technical communication.

title: Multimedia Communications
description:
This course introduces source coding in information theory and its applications to image and video compression. Topics include visual signal characteristics, image/video formats, entropy coding, Huffman coding, arithmetic coding, and CABAC.
For image coding, classical standards such as JBIG, JPEG, and JPEG 2000 will be covered, including prediction, transform coding, quantization, entropy coding, and rate-distortion optimization. Recent developments in deep image compression and JPEG-AI will also be introduced.
For video coding, the course covers H.261, H.263, MPEG-1/2/4, H.264/AVC, H.265/HEVC, and H.266/VVC. Key technologies such as motion estimation, motion compensation, transform coding, in-loop filtering, rate control, scalability, and CABAC will be discussed.
The course also introduces deep video coding, including learned motion estimation, neural motion compensation, end-to-end rate-distortion optimization, and comparisons with traditional hybrid codecs.
Through lectures, standard documents, software demonstrations, and programming assignments, students will gain a theoretical and practical understanding of modern image and video compression technologies.
Course Outline
1. Introductions
2. Multimedia Signals.
3. Information Theory
4. Image Compression/Deep Image Compression
- Transform Coding
- Learned Image Compression
5. Video Coding (H.264/H.266)
- motion estimation/compenstation
- Intra/Inter Frame Coding
- Entropy Coding (CAVLC, CABAC)
- Learned Video Compression
6. Most Recent Deep Video Coding Systems
